Optimal.Notes: Targets a locked 40 fps at 40 Hz for the smoothest practical experience; the EAC anti-cheat issue remains the primary barrier to online play, and this profile assumes a compatible workaround or future fix is in place. In-game setting names are based on standard Apex Legends PC options.

profiles.Summary: Apex Legends is officially unsupported on Steam Deck and is known to have anti-cheat (Easy Anti-Cheat) issues that can prevent online play entirely under Proton, making it effectively unplayable in its live multiplayer mode. Even when it does launch, the fast-paced battle royale gameplay demands consistent frame rates that are difficult to sustain on the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU at native resolution.
profiles.BasisNote: No working Steam Deck player reports exist due to the EAC online block causing the 'Unsupported' rating; profiles are estimated from PC minimum/recommended requirements and Deck hardware capability — if you get the game running, check frame rate in the first full match and lower settings or resolution if it dips below 30 fps.

MaxBattery.Notes: This profile prioritises battery life but the EAC block means online play is likely unavailable; if a workaround is active, expect frame dips in hectic fights even at these settings. In-game setting names are based on standard Apex Legends PC options.

KnownIssues: Easy Anti-Cheat (EAC) blocks online multiplayer under Proton, which is the primary reason for the 'Unsupported' Steam Deck rating — the game may not connect to live servers at all.
EA/Respawn's launcher and account linking can cause additional launch failures or loops before even reaching gameplay.
Performance in busy firefights and high-player-density zones can dip significantly below 30 fps even at low settings.
The game requires a persistent internet connection and EA account; any Proton/network compatibility issues compound the EAC problem.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Even at full TDP and native resolution, 60 fps will not hold consistently in busy combat; expect drops into the 40s during firefights, making a 60 Hz uncapped target aspirational rather than guaranteed. In-game setting names are based on standard Apex Legends PC options.

Optimal.Notes: A locked 40 fps at 40 Hz gives the smoothest feel the Deck can reliably sustain in this title; FSR at 1024x640 recovers visual clarity without tanking the GPU. Use GE-Proton for the best chance of bypassing EAC.

profiles.Summary: Apex Legends is a demanding online-only battle royale that runs with significant caveats on the Steam Deck — Easy Anti-Cheat (EAC) has historically blocked Linux/Proton play, and Valve rates it Unsupported, though some players report silver-level success with GE-Proton. Even when it does launch, the fast-paced gameplay and GPU demands make stable 60 fps difficult, with 40-45 fps at low settings being a more realistic ceiling.
profiles.BasisNote: No current Deck-specific reports were available; profiles are estimated from PC minimum/recommended requirements and Deck hardware capability. On first run, verify EAC allows the game to launch at all, then check frame rate in a hot-drop area and drop to Max Battery if it dips below 30 fps.

MaxBattery.Notes: Renders at sub-native 960x600 with FSR upscaling and an 8 W TDP cap to maximise battery; image quality will be noticeably soft. EAC may prevent the game from launching entirely — if it does not start, no settings changes will help.

KnownIssues: Easy Anti-Cheat (EAC) may block the game from launching entirely under Proton — this is the primary reason for Valve's Unsupported rating.
EA account login and the EA app overlay frequently cause connectivity and authentication issues under Proton.
In-game voice chat and push-to-talk are often non-functional on Linux/Proton.
Trending ProtonDB tier has dropped to bronze, suggesting recent EA app or EAC changes have broken compatibility for many users.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Full TDP and max GPU clock push toward 60 fps but expect drops into the high 40s in busy firefights; battery life will be short. Only worthwhile if EAC is cooperating and you are plugged in or near a charger.
